title: Variance-budgeted autoscaler with deferred burst commitment
author: Priya Desai
commits: init: add variance budget core algorithm and tests
feat: implement deferred burst commitment flow and queueing
chore: wire new metrics to observability and add dashboards
fix: edge-case race in precommit cancellation on node drain
docs: describe config knobs and rollout plan
description:
Context and motivation: We observed recurring SLA blips when tenants with spiky traffic consumed short-lived bursts that later forced aggressive eviction of warm capacity. Existing autoscaler policies allocate headroom primarily from point-in-time utilization and conservative percentiles; they do not explicitly budget for variance in bursty tenants. This PR introduces a variance-budgeted autoscaler policy and a deferred-burst commitment mechanism to reduce unnecessary warm pool churn and preserve throughput guarantees.

What this change does (single-string body): Implements a variance-budgeted allocator that maintains a per-tenant 'variance budget' derived from historical traffic variance and a configurable confidence window. The budget is consumed when a tenant requests burst capacity; instead of committing immediately, the controller places the request into a short deferred-commit queue where capacity checks and global headroom sampling continue for up to a configured grace period (default 6s). If capacity remains available at commit time the burst is finalized; if not, the request is either partially granted (scaled-down commit) or rejected with a clear telemetry event.

Key motivations: 1) Smooth transient overprovisioning spikes that arise from simultaneous microbursts, 2) Preserve guaranteed throughput for steady tenants by avoiding preemptive eviction of long-running reservations, 3) Improve utilization signals by accounting for variance rather than relying solely on fixed percentiles.

Behavioral changes and config knobs: A new policy type 'variance_budget' can be selected per-tenant; parameters added: budget_window_seconds, bootstrap_percentile, commit_grace_seconds, max_partial_commit_ratio. Backwards compatibility: default remains existing percentile-based policy. The deferred commit flow is guarded behind a feature flag (autoscaler.deferred_burst.enabled) to allow staged rollout.

Observability and telemetry: adds metrics: redwood_autoscaler_variance_budget_available, redwood_autoscaler_deferred_queue_length, redwood_autoscaler_deferred_commits_finalized_total, redwood_autoscaler_partial_commits_total, and an event tag 'deferred_burst_rejection_reason'. Dashboards and alert rules added under observability/metrics to highlight growing deferred queue length and sustained budget depletion.

Testing and validation: unit tests for variance_budget math and partial commit scaling added; integration test simulates 200 tenants with randomized microbursts and verifies 95th pct latency and eviction counts do not regress compared to baseline. Local perf runs show ~3% improvement in steady-state utilization for mixed workloads and a 30% reduction in warm-pool churn during synthetic burst storms.

Rollout plan: Enable feature flag in canary clusters for 48 hours with extended telemetry; promote to staging with default budget_window_seconds=300 and commit_grace_seconds=6; observe deferred queue and partial commit metrics for regressions before enabling in production.

Implementation notes and non-obvious details: - Variance budget is maintained as an EWMA of per-tenant short-window variance with a decay that prioritizes recent bursts. - Deferred commit queue is in-memory on the controller and durable across leader elections via small in-cluster lease tokens; commit pre-checks use a sampled lookahead on capacity to avoid over-committing. - To avoid priority inversion we add a soft-fairness gate that prevents long-lived low-priority commit retries from starving new short bursts.

Files changed summary: moved core algorithm into pkg/autoscaler/variance_budget.go; deferred commit state machine in deferred_commit.go; small wiring and config in policy_config.go; controller bootstrap hooks in cmd/controller/main.go; metrics YAML and dashboard scaffolding under observability; integration test and example tenant profile.

Related tickets: ENG-1287 (variance-budget proto and policy), ENG-1310 (deferred commit design spike).

Risks and mitigations: Risk of mis-tuned budgets causing undercommit -> configured conservative bootstrap_percentile and a gradual ramp. Feature flag allows rollback. CI coverage added for the race we observed in drain cancellation.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked and approved - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration test - [x] Metrics and dashboards - [x] Feature flag gating - [x] Rollout plan in PR body

Merge outcome: Squash-merged after two approvals and green CI.
discussion: Aisha: Please add more detail on the EWMA half-life — resolved by making decay configurable and documenting recommended values
Jonah: Concern about controller memory growth with long deferred queues — addressed by bounded queue length with eviction policy and metrics
Marco: Requested an additional integration scenario with node drain during committed bursts — added test case and fixed precommit cancellation race
Author: responded to all review comments, pushed the race fix and extra test, CI flake was re-run once
release_notes: Introduces a variance-budget autoscaling policy and a deferred-burst commitment flow. Feature is off by default and can be enabled via autoscaler.deferred_burst.enabled. Adds new metrics for budget and deferred commit telemetry.
notes_for_ops: Monitor redwood_autoscaler_deferred_queue_length and redwood_autoscaler_variance_budget_available during rollout. Set commit_grace_seconds conservatively for high churn tenants. Use feature flag to rollback instantly.
ci_details: Pipeline: unit -> integration -> e2e. One flaky e2e test (TestWarmPoolStability) rerun and passed on second attempt. Coverage: +3.1% in autoscaler package.
security_considerations: No new external surface. Deferred commit queue state kept in-controller; leader-election durability patterns follow existing lease token approach. No breaking API changes.
how_to_validate: Deploy to staging with feature flag enabled, run workload generator with configured spike pattern, assert no regression in 95th latency and warm-pool eviction counts, verify deferred commit metrics show expected finalization ratio > 80% for benign bursts.
